title: The name that floats over a component can be read
goal: The little label that floats over a component on the canvas, showing its name and which version it is, is dark grey text on a dark chip sitting over a blue shape. It cannot be read. It should be legible over whatever it happens to be sitting on.
notes:
Reported by the user on 2026-09-15 with a screenshot of a chip reading 'Button, rest' floating above a blue rectangle: "i can't even read this, contrast is horrible".

The chip carries the component's name and the version it is showing, which is the thing the shipped task 'a-copy-does-not-say-which-version-it-is-showing' added, so it is new and it arrived unreadable.

The app has solved this problem before for the same reason - a label that has to sit over a picture nobody chose. Measurement chips, caption pills and the name labels over screens all face it, and CanvasNameLabel exists in PhotonzCore. Find what those do and do that, rather than picking a lighter grey and hoping. The acceptance asks for the number because 'looks better' is how this shipped in the first place.

Worth checking while in there whether the same chip is unreadable in light mode as well as dark, since the screenshot is dark and the failure may be the other way round elsewhere.
acceptance: Reproduce it first and measure it: give the contrast ratio of the chip's text against its own background, and against the shapes it sits over
The label is legible over a light shape, a dark shape, a saturated one and a busy screenshot, each captured in the audit
It meets the contrast the rest of the app's canvas chrome is held to, and the audit gives the number rather than saying it looks better
The fix is the one the app already uses for canvas labels that sit over unknown content, rather than a new treatment invented here: say which one was reused
The version part of the label is as readable as the name part, since it is the part that changes and the part somebody is checking
It stays readable at every zoom and on a non-Retina display
Audit under queue/audits/ with the label over four different backgrounds, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Reproduced with Scripts/playtest/version-labels-row-walk.json (real window captures, screen unlocked, Screen Recording granted). Measured from labels-1-four-at-hundred-sc.png: the selected chip's plate is #303030 (L=0.0296) and its text is the accent #3478F6 (L=0.2082) => 3.2:1. The at-rest chip has NO plate at all: violet #A47BF7 (L=0.2877) straight on the picture => 3.1:1 on white canvas, and 1.3:1 on the starter Accent blue #3B7DF5 the buttons are painted in. 1.3:1 is the number behind 'i can't even read this'.

Fix: the chip moved onto the label plate the app already had. LabelPlate (Sources/PhotonzCore/LabelPlate.swift) is AnnotationContent.captionChipColor lifted out of Layer.swift - the measure readout and arrow caption rule, a solid plate in the object's own colour darkened until white reads on it (cap 0.24 luminance), white text, soft shadow. captionChipColor now calls it, so there is one implementation and the two labels cannot drift. Geometry: CanvasNameLabels.plateBox + platePadding (= clearance/2, so two plates can never merge into one bar). Drawing: CanvasComponents.drawNameChip paints the plate for EVERY chip that puts ink down, not only the spelled-out one, and the glyph and the words are both white on it.

Measured off real window captures (Screen Recording granted, screen unlocked), converted P3 to sRGB: the component plate is #503186 and white on it reads 9.88:1 (AAA), IDENTICAL over all four backgrounds - plain light canvas, saturated #FF3B2F shape, deep crimson #AF184A shape, real screenshot - which is the point of a plate. Live/selected: the accent run through the same rule, #00438C, white 9.63:1. Before: violet on the Accent blue a starter button is painted in, 1.0:1.

Adversarial review before building: the mock's own canvas badge (.cbadge in canvas.css) is a solid violet pill with white wording, so the design system already agreed; but white on the token violet #9A5CFF only reaches 3.9:1, so building the mock literally would have shipped a second unreadable label. The app's own rule (darken until white reads) gets 9.9:1 on the same hue. Rejected: picking a lighter violet, which cannot work at all - a label over an unknown picture has no safe ink, which is the whole reason the plate exists.

Verified: Scripts/test.sh green (6910 tests) with 7 new ones - LabelPlateTests pins white-on-plate at 4.5:1 minimum for six colours including white and yellow, at AAA for the component violet, and that the arrow caption chip is the same rule; CanvasNamePlateTests pins the plate geometry and that padding can never exceed the daylight between two names. Walks: new Scripts/playtest/name-chip-reads-anywhere-walk.json (4 backgrounds, the version word, 200%, 50%, light mode) plus component (18), version (7), name (14) and caption (12) families, all green.

left rough: the plate's own edge against a DARK picture is 1.4:1 on the crimson shape, so what separates the pill from the picture there is its shadow and its hue, not its lightness. The words are unaffected at 9.9:1 and it reads in the capture, so it did not earn a task; it is in the audit's rough list for the user to react to.

left rough: two versions of one component landed 34pt apart in my walk, so their drawings and their labels piled up. Not mine and not confirmed broken - version-lands-in-room-walk passes, and in my walk the room around was occupied by a dropped screenshot, which is probably why. Recorded rather than filed.

Filed: a-screen-s-name-can-be-read-over-whatever-it-sit (p2) for the screen name, which has the same fault and was reproduced at 1.9:1 over a crimson shape. Not folded into this task because putting a plate under every frame label changes the look of every canvas, which is a call to make on purpose.

The canvas name chip now sits on the label plate the measure readout and arrow caption already used (LabelPlate in PhotonzCore, lifted out of AnnotationContent.captionChipColor so there is one rule). White on the component plate #503186 reads 9.88:1 AAA, measured off real window captures and identical over a light canvas, a saturated shape, a crimson shape and a real screenshot; live chips use the accent through the same rule at 9.63:1. Was 1.0:1 on the blue a starter button is painted in. Scripts/test.sh green (6910, 7 new), component/version/name/caption walk families green, new walk name-chip-reads-anywhere-walk.json. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-15-canvas-name-chip.json.
